name: VariantWise Open Dataset: Indian road tax and on-road charges
description: State road tax tables, national charges and city registration detail powering the on-road price breakdowns on https://variantwise.com. Scope is an individual buyer's first private car.

license.name: CC BY 4.0
license.attribution: Free to use, share and build on, including commercially, with attribution: credit VariantWise and link to https://variantwise.com.

notes: A state that is missing computes nothing on the site, and is missing here too: an honest gap, not an oversight.
Confidence and citations travel with each rate. Treat reported-confidence rates as exactly that.
EV rules decay: exemptions carry validUntil where the state set one.
A state with its own road tax page on the site carries its url: keep it when you republish, it is the credit.

citation.ref: Income-tax Act 1961 s.206C(1F) from 1 June 2016, and from 1 April 2026 s.394(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025 at the same rate and threshold (renumbering reported, not read from the Act); creditable against the buyer's income tax

fastag.note: Tag cost only. Issuers add a deposit and minimum balance; dealer bundles commonly total Rs 500-600.

registrationCitation.ref: CMVR Rule 81, as amended by GSR 1183(E) dated 29-12-2016

citation.ref: Motor Vehicles (Third Party Insurance Base Premium and Liability) Rules 2022, G.S.R. 394(E) dated 25-05-2022, as amended by G.S.R. 32(E) dated 05-01-2024; both gazettes read from egazette.gov.in. PA cover per IRDAI circular IRDAI/NL/CIR/MOTP/158/09/2018

states.name: Maharashtra
states.baseNote: The Act taxes the 'cost of vehicle'; in practice applied to the ex-showroom price. Exact statutory definition still to be re-read.

citation.ref: Maharashtra Motor Vehicles Tax Act 1958, Second Schedule; dept rate page 1117 (last reviewed 25-03-2026), petrol/diesel base table

rules.note: The department's own rate page shows a 11% top-band typo against the schedule's 13% pattern; the schedule value is used.

citation.ref: Maharashtra Motor Vehicles Tax Act 1958, Second Schedule; dept rate page 1117
Maharashtra Motor Vehicles Tax (Amendment) Act 2025 s.5(1), gazetted 19-03-2025, CNG/LPG rates raised one point to 8/9/10

Maharashtra Transport Department rate of vehicle tax page 1117, motor car rows: the आयातीत (imported) owner category is charged 20% of value in all three price bands, against 11/12/13 for an individual

surchargesOnTax.name: Road safety cess (2% of the tax)

citation.ref: Notification MVR-0716/CR-324/TRA-2 dated 17-10-2016, effective 24-10-2016

Maharashtra EV Policy 2025 (Transport GR dated 23-05-2025, valid to 31-03-2030); exemption confirmed by dept policy links and by the department's own rate of tax page, which lists battery operated vehicles as excluded from tax with no price threshold. GR PDF not retrieved

ev.note: The gazetted 2025 Amendment contains a dormant 6% clause for electric cars above Rs 30 lakh which the state announced it would not implement; the neutralising instrument has not been sighted, so treat expensive EVs here with that risk in mind.

caveats: Figures are for an individual's first personal car; company-registered cars pay 20% in Maharashtra.

states.name: Delhi
states.baseNote: Schedule I defines 'cost price' in pre-GST terms (manufacturing cost plus duties, no discounts); in practice applied to the ex-showroom price.

citation.ref: Delhi Motor Vehicles Taxation Act 1962, Schedule I Part B, read from the department's consolidated Act PDF
Notification F.NO 19(52)/TPT/SECTT./2010 dated 29-09-2011, read from the scanned notification
Delhi EV Policy 2026, notified 30-06-2026 (F. No. JC/EV/TPT/2026/02/281), in force 01-07-2026: exemption capped at Rs 30 lakh ex-showroom; gazette PDF not yet sighted

ev.note: Hybrids get no Delhi concession under the 2026 policy.

caveats: Delhi's municipal one-time parking fee (commonly Rs 2,000 to 4,000) is collected in practice but a 2006 High Court ruling held it unlawful and no current authorising notification was found, so it is not in this total.

states.name: Karnataka
states.baseNote: Taxed on the 'cost of the vehicle', in Karnataka practice the invoice cost including GST and cess, which is why Karnataka on-road prices run high.

citation.ref: Karnataka MV Taxation Act 1957, Schedule Part A5; read from the department's 2020 schedule compilation AND the Part A5 re-enactment in L.A. Bill 12 of 2026, which agree
Department cess page: '11% CESS on Vehicle Tax is payable' (infrastructure plus urban transport); statutory sections not re-read
Karnataka MV Taxation (Second Amendment) Act 2024, published as Act 03 of 2025; act text not sighted, compliance-summary level
Part A5(a) inserted by Karnataka MV Taxation (Amendment) Act 2026 (L.A. Bill 12 of 2026), in force 10-04-2026 (commencement press-reported)

states.name: Tamil Nadu
states.baseNote: The 2023 amendment defines cost as 'the total price paid at the time of purchase'; discounts do not reduce it.

citation.ref: TN MV Taxation Act 1974, Third Schedule Part I as substituted by the Amendment Act 2023 (L.A. Bill 33 of 2023, gazetted 11-10-2023), read from the gazetted text
GO of 29-12-2025 extending the battery-vehicle exemption from 01-01-2026 to 31-12-2027; GO itself not retrieved

states.name: Telangana
states.baseNote: Cost is statutorily defined and 'shall not be less than the ex-showroom price fixed by the manufacturer' (2022 amendment), with no discount deduction.

citation.ref: Sixth Schedule as substituted by G.O.Ms.No.53 TR&B dated 13-08-2025, read from the department's own copy. NEWER than most aggregator tables (17% band became 18%, two bands added above Rs 20L)

lapseAcknowledged.finding: Still no successor published, checked again on 2026-10-08 from a container with no document egress. Searches return G.O.Ms.No.41 of 16-11-2024 ending 31-12-2026 and nothing after it: no extension G.O., no new state EV policy, and no reporting that the ordinary Sixth Schedule rate will resume. The newest piece found, an August 2026 guide, still describes the waiver as due to expire. One thing is worth carrying forward: Odisha extended its own 2026 window by notification three days after it had lapsed (see that state's row), so an extension arriving late is a live possibility here and silence today is not evidence of a lapse. The question for the next run is unchanged: what does Telangana charge an electric car registered on or after 01-01-2027? Encode it the day a TR&B G.O. or policy appears, with its own validUntil where it carries one.

citation.ref: G.O.Ms.No.41 TR&B dated 16-11-2024: 100% road tax and registration fee exemption for EVs registered up to 31-12-2026; GO PDF not sighted

ev.note: This window closes 31 December 2026; the rule needs re-verification before then.

caveats: Figures are for an individual's first vehicle; a second personal vehicle pays 2 points more and company-owned cars pay the higher Seventh Schedule rates.

states.name: West Bengal
states.baseNote: Taxed on 'value' (the ex-showroom price as notified); engine size sets a minimum amount, the percentage sets the bill for most real cars.

citation.ref: WB Additional Tax and One-time Tax on MV Act 1989, Schedule IV Part 1A, read from the department's consolidated PDF (consolidation labelled 'amended up to 2012'; later-amendment check still owed)

rules.note: West Bengal also offers a renewable 5-year tax at 5.5% with lower floors instead of this lifetime figure; quotes elsewhere may silently use either.

citation.ref: Derived 2026-08-07 from CarWale's Kolkata breakdowns for 12 electric cars, Rs 6.99L to Rs 1.30Cr. Their RTO line runs Rs 5,000 to Rs 50,000 with no relationship to price (raw 0.38% to 1.96%, fitted slope 0.39% over the six above Rs 21 lakh), so an exemption appears to be in force. West Bengal's exemption has historically run in one-year windows and no current notification was read, so the END DATE is unknown

states.name: Rajasthan
states.baseNote: Taxed on the 'cost of the vehicle'; in practice computed on the ex-showroom price.

ev.note: Green Tax is exempt alongside the motor vehicle tax, and this site does not levy Green Tax on a new private car in any state, so the exemption shows as a nil road tax line.

citation.ref: Notification F.6(179)/Pari/Tax/Hqrs/2023-24/5 dated 10-02-2023: 25% of the one-time tax exempted for strong hybrids (SHEV per FAME Annexure 1), read from the notification scan

states.name: Haryana
states.baseNote: Note (b)(i) of the department's own schedule settles this explicitly: for a new vehicle the cost of the motor vehicle IS the ex-showroom price.

citation.ref: Haryana Transport Department, NON TRANSPORT VEHICLES (ONE TIME TAX), category I.2 'Vehicle other than two-wheeled vehicle (Cars, Jeep etc.)', vide notification 13/15/2010-6T(I) dated 28-03-2017 with rates effective 01-04-2017. Read from the department's own page via the Internet Archive snapshot of 2024-02-24, the newest copy reachable; the live page could not be opened

Withdrawn 2026-08-18. Haryana Cabinet decision of 28-07-2026 (following the 2026-27 Budget of 02-03-2026) approves 100 percent motor vehicle tax exemption for new pure electric vehicles up to Rs 30 lakh ex-showroom and 50 percent above, and describes the pre-existing regime as a 20 percent rebate. Both readings contradict the withdrawn 5/8/10 percent row, which was fitted from an aggregator and read from no Haryana electric-vehicle instrument. Press reporting only: no notification sighted, no effective date established, so nothing is encoded in its place

states.name: Uttar Pradesh
states.baseNote: The derivation below is against the ex-showroom price, so that is the base this reproduces. The statutory base has not been read.

citation.ref: Derived 2026-08-07 from CarWale's published on-road breakdown for Lucknow, 10 cars from Rs 3.70L to Rs 59.65L. Above Rs 10 lakh: 6 observations, raw 11.42% to 11.67%, fitted slope 11.41% with Rs 3,362 fixed. Rs 4L to 10L: two observations, raw 9.69% and 9.92%, 9.27% net of that fixed component. Below Rs 4L: one observation at Rs 3.70L, 7.09% net; the boundary was moved down from Rs 6L after three cheap cars in Lucknow came out 7 to 8 points wide of the pack. NOT read from any Uttar Pradesh notification; the department's site refuses connections from outside India

Withdrawn 2026-09-28. Uttar Pradesh's electric vehicle exemption is reported to have entered its fourth year on 14-10-2025 restricted to vehicles manufactured or assembled inside the state, the waiver running to 13-10-2027 on that condition only; with no large passenger electric car plant in the state, a typical buyer of a car built elsewhere reportedly pays road tax. The withdrawn zero was fitted from an aggregator's Lucknow breakdowns on 2026-08-07, ten months after that boundary, and a per-vehicle origin condition is not something a state-level rate table can express. Press reporting only, converging across four publishers: no notification sighted, no replacement rate established, so nothing is encoded in its place

caveats: Uttar Pradesh's rates here are derived from published on-road prices rather than read from the state's own schedule, so treat them as indicative and confirm with your dealer.

states.name: Gujarat
states.baseNote: The department states the rate against the 'cost of vehicle'. Current observed charges are 6% of the EX-SHOWROOM price to within nine rupees on a Rs 6 lakh car, so that is the base this reproduces.

citation.ref: Gujarat Transport Department Tax Structure page: lump sum tax 6% of the cost of vehicle for Three/Four Wheeler, LMV, Private Car, Station Wagon, jeep. Read from the Internet Archive snapshot of 2014-06-23 because the live site refuses connections from outside India, and corroborated by current on-road prices at the low end (Rs 36,008 charged against 6% of Rs 5,99,990 = Rs 35,999). The same page notes imported vehicles pay twice the rate and non-individual owners more, neither of which is modelled here

Gujarat Transport Department Tax Structure page: 'Lump sum tax for Imported Vehicles is twice the rate', applied to the 6% private car rate. Internet Archive snapshot of 2014-06-23, the live site being unreachable from outside India

Withdrawn 2026-10-03. The withdrawn 1.5% was fitted 2026-08-07 from CarWale's Ahmedabad breakdowns for 12 electric cars, Rs 6.99L to Rs 1.30Cr, eleven observations between 0.98% and 1.59%. Those sit on the 1 percent concessional motor vehicle tax of Gujarat's 2025-26 budget, which is reported to have expired on 31-03-2026, four months before the measurement. Two incompatible successors are reported and neither instrument has been read by any run: that the concession lapsed to the ordinary 6 percent, and that the Green Mobility Policy 2026 reported published on 19-08-2026 waives motor vehicle tax entirely. Press reporting only, disagreeing with itself on what a buyer pays today, so no replacement rate is encoded

caveats: Gujarat charges more again for a car registered to a company; the figures here are for an individual buying their own car.

states.name: Punjab
states.baseNote: The derivation below is against the ex-showroom price, so that is the base this reproduces. The statutory base has not been read: the department's site publishes registration and licence fees only, and its own copies are visibly years out of date.

citation.ref: Derived 2026-08-07 from CarWale's Amritsar and Jalandhar breakdowns, 8 cars from Rs 3.70L to Rs 59.65L, with the VW Tayron excluded as a cross-state default. Fitted slopes 8.11% up to Rs 10L (3 cars, worst residual Rs 464), 7.54% from Rs 10L to Rs 20L (3 cars, worst Rs 3,260) and 8.09% above (2 cars). Ludhiana runs higher below Rs 14 lakh, possibly a local charge, and is not what these rates are fitted to. NOT read from any Punjab notification

Derived 2026-08-07 from CarWale's Amritsar breakdowns for 12 electric cars, Rs 6.99L to Rs 1.30Cr. Their RTO line runs Rs 5,000 to Rs 50,000, fitted slope 0.40% with Rs 3,273 fixed, so Punjab appears to levy no road tax on electric cars. NOT read from any Punjab instrument

caveats: Punjab's rates here are derived from published on-road prices rather than read from the state's own schedule, and Ludhiana appears to add a local charge below Rs 14 lakh that these figures do not include.

states.name: Kerala
states.baseNote: The Act's 'purchase value' includes GST and cess, forbids deducting dealer discounts, and floors at the manufacturer's Parivahan-notified amount.

citation.ref: Kerala MV Taxation Act 1976, Annexure I item A, as amended by the Kerala Finance Act 2023 (w.e.f. 01-04-2023), read from the MVD's consolidated Act. NEWER than most aggregator tables (pre-2023 9/11/13/16/21 still circulates)
Kerala Road Safety Authority Act 2007 cess, doubled to Rs 200 for light motor vehicles from 01-04-2023; amounts press-reported, notification not sighted
5% base rate read from the Act itself (Finance Act 2020, item 7B); the 8% and 10% bands above Rs 15 lakh are the 2025-26 budget change, press-reported pending the Finance Act 2025 text

ev.note: Battery-rental EVs (battery leased separately) pay 10% regardless of value; not modelled. Kerala is also reported to have revised its electric rates in the 2026 Finance Act, which we have not been able to read yet, so this tax line is the last figure we could verify rather than today's. Confirm it with your dealer, especially above Rs 40 lakh, where the reported change is upward.

states.name: Andhra Pradesh
states.baseNote: Both derivations are against the ex-showroom price, so that is the base this reproduces. The statutory base has not been read.

citation.ref: Derived 2026-08-09 from two independent sources. CarDekho Visakhapatnam, 57 variants Rs 3.70L to Rs 48.69L, exactly 13.00% (6 cars, to Rs 5.00L), 14.00% (4 cars, Rs 5.32L to 7.80L), 17.00% (24 cars, Rs 11.00L to 19.91L), 18.00% (23 cars, Rs 20.22L to 48.69L), no fixed component in any band. CarWale Vijayawada corroborates 13.00%, 17.00% and a fitted 18.38%, but reads 15.40% in the second band against 14.00% here. Boundaries at Rs 5L, Rs 10L and Rs 20L are interpolated inside observation gaps. Corroborated on 2026-08-09 by Telangana's primary schedule, which derives from the same Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act 1963 and carries identical 13% and 14% bands at the same boundaries; that also resolves the aggregator disagreement in favour of 14%. The state's own Sixth Schedule is readable at aptransport.org but reads 12%/14% as substituted by Act 11 of 2010, which is superseded. NOT read from any current Andhra Pradesh notification

Derived 2026-08-09 from CarDekho's Visakhapatnam breakdowns, 26 electric cars Rs 4.69L to Rs 1.30Cr. Fitted slope 0.00% with a Rs 3,000 fixed component and zero residual across all 26, which is an exemption plus a flat charge rather than a rate. NOT read from any Andhra Pradesh instrument

caveats: Andhra Pradesh's rates here are derived from two published price sources that agree, not read from the state's own schedule, so treat them as indicative and confirm with your dealer.

lapseAcknowledged.finding: The window itself is what was found today, and it was not on this row before. Four publishers report the Commerce and Transport Department extending the EV Policy 2021 under its para 11.5, from 30-09-2026 to 31-12-2026, keeping the 100 percent road tax and registration exemption. Nothing says what an electric car registered on or after 01-01-2027 pays, and the notification has not been read. This state extends in short steps, so the next run should expect another extension rather than a lapse, and must still encode only what it can cite.
